newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden will lose influence outside EMU, Asbrink says.
newsitem.headline: Sweden will lose influence outside EMU, Asbrink says.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Wednesday that Sweden would lose influence in Europe as a result of refusing to adhere to the EU's economic and monetary union at its 1999 launch.
"We can't be part of the decision-making process in a club where we are not members," Asbrink told Swedish television after Sweden decided not to immediately join the EU's single currency.
But Asbrink said other EU nations understood why the government -- facing strong anti-EMU public opinion -- had decided to stay outside.

"My impression is that there is understanding for the situation in Sweden. I have had lots of contact with my EU colleagues and I know what they think. There will certainly be some critical comments but we have to accept that.

The ruling Social Democratic Party's executive committee ruled on Tuesday that Sweden would not join EMU at its planned launch in 1999 but kept the door open for joining before parliamentary elections due in 2002.
